overall.release_block_reason: The unified API is complete, but donor redistribution rights, credential rotation, project licensing, frontend semantics and hardening remain open.

last_event.message: The production application now mounts a versioned API backed by explicit observation, integration-status and canonical research-readiness facades; offline, OpenAPI and negative execution-surface contracts passed Phase 3 acceptance.

notes: Pytest cache writes were disabled for the acceptance run; no cache warning was emitted.
Playwright verified the static projection on desktop and mobile and confirmed offline requests reset all displayed evidence to BLOCK.
Donor credential findings are not included in values or logs; two credentials require owner rotation.
Phase 2 added 226 passing yeuxQ tests with three Windows symlink-permission skips, plus three passing Rust tests.
Python is canonical by default; Rust is development-only, explicitly selected and falls back without exposing internal errors.
A wheel-like extraction smoke test served the packaged Web UI and kept writable data outside site-packages.
The production app mounts only bounded v1 observation, integration-status and canonical readiness facades; OpenAPI contains no account, broker, order, cancel, trade or execution endpoint.
The complete Python regression passed 1266 tests with three Windows symlink-permission skips; one Starlette TestClient deprecation warning remains tracked for hardening.

phases.name: Repository and compliance audit
acceptance: Canonical, donor and reference-only roles are fixed.
Secrets, runtime artifacts and license risks are inventoried without copying their contents.
No donor or v4 directory was bulk-copied into the canonical repository.
phases.notes: Audit completion is an inventory milestone, not license clearance or strategy approval.

phases.name: Architecture, contracts, compliance and status UI baseline
release_blockers_outside_phase: Rotate the two real credentials detected in the donor local intel configuration without copying or exposing them.
Record the user's project LICENSE decision or keep release blocked.
acceptance: Canonical serialization and SHA-256 are deterministic.
Tampering, duplicate IDs and path escape fail closed.
Research-only and no-broker invariants are mandatory fields.
Repository secret scan passes and synthetic leak fixtures are detected.
Status JSON parses and unsupported schema versions fail closed.

phases.name: Controlled stock_v2 application and observation migration
acceptance: Provider failures, rate limits, stale cache and unavailable capabilities are explicit.
Observation storage is physically separate from research storage.
No provider path can write to the research database.
Optional Rust failure falls back to a tested Python implementation.

phases.name: Unified API and research facade
acceptance: Versioned API uses public contracts and read-only research facades.
No account, broker, order, cancel or live-execution endpoint exists.
File access is allowlisted and path traversal is rejected.
Offline startup and OpenAPI contract tests pass.

phases.name: Clean-room frontend and continuous status UI
acceptance: UI status matches this JSON and shows invalid state as BLOCK.
Observation source, timestamps, freshness and unavailable state are visible.
Observation signals, research gates and paper simulation are visually distinct.
No v4 expressive code or assets are reused.

phases.name: Research integration and regression hardening
acceptance: Existing quantify regression suite passes.
Observation cannot upgrade research gates.
Donor backtest and LLM outputs remain advisory only.
Python and optional Rust parity tests pass.
All P0 risks are closed.

phases.name: Release, migration and donor deprecation
acceptance: Clean checkout install, test, startup and UI smoke pass.
Project LICENSE and third-party notices are complete.
CI enforces lint, tests, secrets and license checks.
Local, remote and UI commit SHA agree.
Donor is read-only and canonical is the only release source.

risks.title: Donor redistribution rights are not established
risks.closure: Obtain rights confirmation or use only clean-room rewrites with per-file provenance.

risks.title: v4 license-bound and vendored material could be copied accidentally
risks.closure: Keep reference-only controls and staged-content scans passing through release.

risks.title: Donor local configuration contains real LLM or MCP credentials
risks.closure: Rotate credentials and prove ignore plus secret scanner coverage without exposing values.

risks.title: Live observations could contaminate research data or evidence
risks.closure: Independent append-only observation storage, explicit capture and negative promotion-boundary tests are in place; retain them through full hardening before closing.

risks.title: Trend plans or predictions could be interpreted as live trading instructions
risks.closure: Lock contract, API and UI to research-only with no broker or order capability.

risks.title: Duplicate backtests or gates could issue contradictory promotion results
risks.closure: The v1 research facade reads only canonical src/quantify readiness artifacts and strips donor, LLM and observation promotion fields; retain negative tests through hardening before closing.

risks.title: Frontend integration progress could diverge from repository evidence
risks.closure: Validate and project this file read-only; commit status updates with implementation and tests.

risks.title: Symbol and exchange normalization may diverge
risks.closure: Use canonical SymbolId and cross-market fixtures.

risks.title: Timezone, calendar, adjustment and suspension semantics may diverge
risks.closure: Publish a data dictionary and pass boundary fixtures.

risks.title: Stale provider cache may be displayed as real-time
risks.closure: Provider TTL and HIT/MISS/STALE reasons are explicit; complete visible freshness QA in the unified frontend before closing.

risks.title: SQLite locking and schema evolution may be unsafe
risks.closure: Separate databases, version schemas and pass concurrency plus recovery tests.

risks.title: Python and Rust analysis may drift
risks.closure: Pass parity fixtures and retain deterministic Python fallback.

risks.title: File, URL or rich-text API surfaces may be exploitable
risks.closure: Report paths are allowlisted, traversal is rejected, no arbitrary proxy is exposed and packaged rich text uses DOMPurify; re-audit the versioned API and frontend before closing.

risks.title: Third-party web dependency notices may be incomplete
risks.closure: Bundled web dependencies have pinned versions, SHA-256 values, upstream sources and SPDX notices; retain automated manifest verification through release.

risks.title: Donor runtime or build artifacts could leak into Git
risks.closure: Enforce denylist, ignore rules and staged artifact scans.

risks.title: Documentation or UI may overstate real-time capability
risks.closure: Review capability matrix, fallback semantics and research-only wording.

next_actions.action: Confirm redistribution rights for the donor source or replace source-derived files with independently authorized clean-room implementations.
Rotate the two donor-exposed credentials without copying or displaying their values.
Ask the repository owner to choose the project LICENSE or retain release BLOCK.
Connect the clean-room workbench to v1 facades and label buy, sell and scan outputs as bounded analysis rather than trading instructions.
Keep legacy micro-live readiness semantics behind the canonical offline research boundary and add negative exposure tests before release.
